objective: Enter the Wigley parabolic hull as the naval line's calm-water entry case, on the grounds that its geometry is an algebraic expression rather than a file anyone has to be given, and settle at zero compute whether its openly downloadable primary reference tabulation is internally consistent enough to grade against before any free-surface mesh is bought
rationale: The naval line's blocking lesson is that excellent reference data does not imply obtainable geometry: a hull with tank data across eleven facilities has no verified open geometry route here, its navy host resolving nowhere, one workshop registration-walled and another failing on a certificate mismatch. The Wigley hull is the exact inverse structure and that is the whole argument for it. ITS GEOMETRY IS A CLOSED-FORM EXPRESSION: the half-breadth is the product of a parabola in the longitudinal coordinate and a parabola in the vertical, so the surface is generated by arithmetic on the machine that will mesh it. There is no download, no host, no certificate and no registration in the geometry half at all, which removes the entire failure mode that stopped the previous hull. THE REFERENCE HALF, VERIFIED BY MACHINE FETCH ON 2026-08-14: the summary report of the Japanese cooperative experiment on the Wigley parabolic model, prepared for the seventeenth towing tank conference resistance committee in 1983, is held in an open internet archive mirror of a defence technical information record and was downloaded here in full, HTTP 200, 2,376,271 bytes, no credential and no registration. It was converted to text and searched: it carries total resistance, frictional resistance, wave resistance and wave pattern resistance for four geosim models of 6.0, 4.0, 2.5 and 2.0 metres, and it carries an explicit numbered table of NONDIMENSIONAL WAVE ELEVATION ON THE HULL for three of them. AND ONE HONEST DEFECT, STATED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED LATER: the document is a 1983 scan and its text layer is badly recovered. The table's numerals come out of the text layer garbled and interleaved. The data is present as a TABLE and not as a figure, which is strictly better than the dam-break reference this lab currently grades a naval verdict against and which it obtained by digitising a secondary source's picture twice. But it must be read off the page image by a human or a careful reader, not scraped, and this proposal says so before anyone budgets for scraping it. THE NULL, AND IT IS NOT FITTED: the tabulated experimental wave elevation and resistance, taken from a document written 43 years ago by four laboratories that have never heard of this one. THE IDENTITY TEST, owner rule W dash 2: the stage 1 gate below is a cross-model consistency test on the reference itself, and the question is whether agreement between the geosim models could be true by construction. It could not, and the reason is physical rather than rhetorical: the four models are separate physical hulls towed in separate tanks, and the nondimensionalisation that makes them comparable divides wave elevation by model length, which is exactly the quantity that differs between them. If a scale effect existed at the graded stations, the nondimensional profiles would separate. Agreement is therefore informative and disagreement is informative, which is what the earlier correlation failure in this lab did not have when its own null sat pinned at unity.
gate: STAGE 1, ZERO COMPUTE, AND IT IS ALLOWED TO KILL STAGE 2. Read the tabulated nondimensional wave elevation off the page images for the 6.0, 4.0 and 2.5 metre models at the Froude numbers the document tabulates, transcribe them twice independently, and reconcile the two transcriptions before anything else is done with them. Then the three-valued verdict on the REFERENCE, not on any solver. PASS, reference usable, if the three geosim models agree at every tabulated station within the spread the document itself reports for repeat runs, and if the two independent transcriptions agree to the last printed digit. FAIL, reference not gradeable, if the geosim models separate by more than the resistance tolerance any calm-water gate would use, because a reference carrying scale effect larger than the gate band cannot decide the gate and the case must be entered on resistance alone or not at all. NO VERDICT if the scan cannot be read at a station, reported station by station rather than as a whole-table judgement. STAGE 2, NOT REQUESTED HERE: a calm-water resistance ladder. It is named only so the sequencing argument is checkable. WHAT THIS GATE IS NOT: it does not test any turbulence model, any mesh or any solver, and it may not be reported as validating one.
cost_basis: ZERO solver compute. Scored in agent tool calls because the core-minute unit carries no information for this item. Forecast 30 calls, at the low end of this lab's measured build-and-verify band of 33 to 72 and above its bounded-question band of 2 to 5, because the document is already downloaded and the work is transcription and arithmetic rather than acquisition. The actual will be counted from the executing agent's transcript and written back as a measured tool call count. The purchase this displaces is stated so the comparison is real: the marine line's next-cheapest calm-water hull item is priced at 3000 core minutes with an explicitly unanchored basis by its own author, and its own author recommends buying a 450 core-minute feasibility slice first. A hull whose geometry costs nothing to obtain is the cheaper feasibility slice, and this item prices the reference question underneath it at zero.
expected_knowledge_gain: THE DISCRIMINATING OUTCOME. Belief moves either way. If the geosim models agree, the naval line gains an entry case with an analytically generated geometry and a primary tabulated reference, which is a strictly stronger provenance position than either hull currently on the board, and the standing block on the naval ladder stops being a block on the whole line because a second, independent calm-water rung exists beside it. If they disagree, the finding is that the classical hull reference carries scale effect at the graded quantity, which is a real and citable result about a benchmark many groups grade against, and it steers this lab off wave-profile grading and onto resistance. The one outcome that moves nothing is a scan too poor to read at any station, and that is reported as a gap map row naming which stations were lost.
hard_criterion_note: Criterion 4, free surface. The case the reference exists to grade is a hull generating a wave system that the solver has to capture. Stage 1 as requested starts no flow case and is arithmetic over a downloaded document.
